title: Generalized Coordinate Bethe Ansatz and Quantum Integrability of the Time-Dependent Massive Thirring Model
abstract: We develop a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework for the massive Thirring model with an explicitly time-dependent fermion mass. Unlike the generalized Bethe ansatz for chiral quantum field theories, where particle transport acts in internal spin spaces and leads to quantum Knizhnik-Zamolodchikov equations, the present construction acts directly on particle coordinates and physical rapidities. Its central new feature is a rapidity lattice. Because the time-dependent mass couples right- and left-moving components already in the one-particle sector, a fixed-rapidity block is not closed under spatial winding. Periodicity therefore requires all sectors generated by the finite shift $β\toβ-p$. Particle exchange relates amplitudes on this lattice through scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type, whose solutions determine the complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction. Consistency of the coordinate construction also selects an exponential evolution of the bare mass, providing a new realization of the time dependent integrability-renormalization group correspondence. In the static limit, the rapidity-lattice construction reduces to the conventional massive-Thirring Bethe equations. Through the massive-Thirring/sine Gordon equivalence, the result also connects this exact quantum construction to the generalized space-time dependent Lax formalism.
summary: This work presents a generalized coordinate Bethe ansatz for the massive Thirring model with a time-varying mass. By developing a framework based on a unique rapidity lattice, the authors solve for the exact time-dependent many-body wavefunction. This provides a new, coordinate-space realization of the time-dependent integrability-RG correspondence.
main_problem: The paper develops a generalized coordinate Bethe-ansatz framework to solve the massive Thirring model when the fermion mass is explicitly time-dependent.
main_result: The construction successfully yields the many-body wavefunction on a discrete rapidity lattice, establishing a novel coordinate route to the time-dependent integrability-RG correspondence.
method: The method involves constructing the wavefunction using a generalized coordinate Bethe ansatz, leading to scalar analytic difference equations of Ruijsenaars type.
model_or_system: The system is the massive Thirring model, characterized by a Hamiltonian containing a time-dependent fermion mass, $m_b(t)$. The analysis is performed on a circle of circumference L.
key_observables: The complete time-dependent many-body wavefunction, and the exponential evolution of the bare mass, $m_b(t) = m^*e^{\kappa t}$.
important_parameters: The time-dependent mass $m_b(t)$, the coupling constant $g_0$, and the rapidity lattice structure.
main_assumptions: The construction is fundamentally different from chiral theories because the mass term couples right- and left-moving components directly in the one-particle sector, necessitating the rapidity lattice.
paper_structure: The paper builds the solution by first establishing the coordinate Bethe ansatz structure, deriving the two-particle S-matrix, and then using this to construct the full N-particle wavefunction on the rapidity lattice. It compares this to the static limit and relates the structure to known integrable formalisms.
why_interesting: The focus on time-dependent integrability and the connection to RG flow provides a powerful, non-equilibrium tool for analyzing quantum field theories, which has parallels in non-equilibrium dynamics studied in AMO and condensed matter.
